scenario: AITA got refusing to back up for someone who drove the wrong way up to an ATM? | My bank has kind of an odd set up for their ATM out front. It’s in a small cut out with clearly marked arrows pointing to which way the entrance is, in addition to the fact that since this is a drive up ATM it makes sense for the machine to be on the left side where the driver would be sitting. That said, it’s very easy for people to turn I to the outcropping the wrong way. This happened today while I went to get some cash. I arrived at my bank and as I took the turn to go into the ATM cut out, another car whipped into it going the wrong way so that their passenger could use the ATM. I was annoyed at this as I was just about to pull up to it and I was in kind of a hurry, since I needed to get to class. She took 15 minutes to do her transactions. She went through at least 3 cards inserting and reinserting the cards at least 2 times each. I sat patiently, yet annoyed, and waited for her to finish. But when she was done was reaching my limit of patience, she then leant out the window of her car and yell at me to move, I didn’t respond, no one was waiting behind me, I had already been late to class, so being more late wouldn’t kill me. I didn’t move. After about 5 minutes of her shouting at me to move, she backed up did a K-turn and left. I told my friend about this when I eventually arrived at class and he told me that I was being a dick for not just backing up since there was no one behind me. However I stick to the notion that I was in the right for not moving because they were going against traffic. AITA?

Wearing a suit and tie makes me feel confident. What do you think?

It’s great to hear that a suit and tie boost your confidence! The way we dress can have a powerful psychological impact—often called the “enclothed cognition” effect. When you put on a garment that signals professionalism, authority, or success, it can actually shift your mindset and make you feel more capable and self-assured. Here are a few reasons why a suit and tie might feel so empowering: | Why it works | How it shows up | |--------------|-----------------| | **Social cues** | People often associate suits with competence and leadership, so you may feel you’re meeting those expectations. | | **Self‑perception** | Dressing up can reinforce a personal identity of being “serious” or “prepared.” | | **Physical posture** | A tailored suit encourages a straighter posture, which can improve breathing and reduce stress. | | **Attention to detail** | The effort you put into looking sharp can translate into a sense of control over your environment. | If you’re looking to extend that confidence into other areas, you might try: 1. **Pair it with a personal mantra** – a quick affirmation (“I’m ready to tackle this”) right before you step out. 2. **Practice power poses** – standing tall for a minute can boost cortisol and testosterone levels. 3. **Set a small goal** – e.g., “I’ll introduce myself to one new person today.” The suit can be the catalyst for taking that step. Do you find that the confidence lasts throughout the day, or does it fade after a while? And are there particular situations where the suit feels especially powerful? Knowing more about when and why it works can help you harness that feeling even more effectively.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?
